messages:
jonah: FYI, my terraform plan for the GPU nodepool size got blocked by Conftest during pre-merge checks. PR: https://git.company/repo/infra/pull/4321 :eyes:

maria: ugh — what rule failed? paste the conftest output?

jonah: here's the failure snippet from CI:
```
WARN: policy violation - rule 'no-unapproved-gpu'
msg: "GPU pool size changes require freeze-window approval or an exception from infra-approvers"
resource: module/gpu/node_pool.tf
```

infra-bot: Policy check failed: https://ci.company/builds/98765 (rule: no-unapproved-gpu) :no_entry_sign:

kirti: We're inside the infra freeze window until 2026-03-20 23:59 for changes that touch GPU capacity. Exceptions are allowed but need two infra-approver signatures + SRE review.

sam: Are we able to avoid the tf change and do a runtime scale instead? e.g., use the burst-pool config or temporarily increase quota via provider? That avoids changing managed nodepool sizing in gitops.

jonah: The change is to bump `replica_count` and GPU type for a dedicated pool (NVIDIA A100 -> A10G) for a new workload. Runtime scaling won't help because it's a pool sizing + instance-type swap.

maria: Cost + quota note: eu-west1 quota for A100s is already fully committed under our team quotas. If we change instance type to A10G we still hit regional quota approval. That might need cloud quota request (2-3 business days).

kirti: Given that, two safe options: 1) request a temporary exception for this PR (infra-approvers only) if it's urgent; 2) do a canary in a different region or a CPU fallback pool and iterate. Which do we prefer?

jonah: Urgency: product wants >10k throughput next week. Canary in a different region is risky due to data locality. We should try exception path first. How do we raise it from the PR?

nina: File an infra-exception ticket in Jira with the link to the PR, cost impact, rollback plan, and mitigations. Add label `gpu-exception` and ping @kirti @sam for approval. I can triage SRE review once ticket exists.

sam: +1. Also include a short runbook snippet for rollback and node drain commands. Example:
```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
terraform apply -target=module.gpu.node_pool
```

maria: one more ask: include a post-deploy rollout plan in the ticket (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 24h) and cost estimate for the delta. Ops likes numbers.

jonah: I'll open the ticket now and link back here. If approvals come thru, can we exempt Conftest for this PR temporarily or will the CI block it regardless?

kirti: CI will still block. Once ticket is approved, infra SRE can add a per-PR override tag in the policy engine (short-lived) and we re-run the pipeline. We'll document the override id in the ticket.

maria: tagging for visibility: @infra-approvers please review when ticket lands. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: New ticket created: INFRA-EXC-214 (linked PR: https://git.company/repo/infra/pull/4321). Current status: awaiting approver signatures.

jonah: thanks all — I'll include the cost estimate and rollback steps. Will update in ~30m.

sam: if we need a faster path later, we can also consider a temporary dedicated quota on Redwood Dedicated where possible, but that requires procurement + billing signoff.

kirti: noted. let's try the exception flow first. If quota blocks, we'll explore the Dedicated burst option.

jonah: updated ticket with numbers and rollout plan: https://jira.company/browse/INFRA-EXC-214 (pinged approvers).

maria: good work, keep the SRE postmortem checklist ready in case of regression. :eyes:
